### Corrections and new evidence gathered during remediation

1. **FE-MED-3, corrected.** The claim "copy/paste of a user's own data is broken by default" was **too broad**. Live verification shows the reader content resolves to `user-select: text` (an ancestor applies `select-text`) and programmatic selection returns text. Only application chrome resolves to `user-select: none`. The residual issue is chrome text (titles, annotation quotes) — a polish item, not a blocker.
2. **FE-MED-2, confirmed live.** The dev build fetched `fonts.googleapis.com` CSS **and** `fonts.gstatic.com` `woff2` files, while the packaged CSP (`default-src 'self'`, no `font-src`) blocks both. The dev/prod divergence and the third-party request at launch are both verified, not inferred.
3. **FE-09, confirmed live (new evidence).** The running app fetched cover images from `images.unsplash.com` (two failed with `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB`). Remote image loading is live in this codebase, which is what makes the CSP's `img-src … https:` a real privacy surface rather than a theoretical one.
4. **New token defect found and fixed.** `<body>` carried hardcoded `bg-[#FAF7F2] text-[#1C1917]` utility classes; a class selector outranks the `body` element rule, so `--bg-primary`/`--text-primary` were silently ineffective on the root element (dark mode's body background stayed light, masked only by the app containers painting over it). Verified fixed: `rgb(24,24,27)` in dark mode.
5. **One unreproduced observation, reported rather than claimed.** During scripted preview interaction the reader appeared to close itself and the library section changed on its own once; it did not reproduce in repeated attempts (the reader then stayed open for the full observation window) and it is not consistent with any code path found. Most likely an artifact of the scripted clicks. Worth instrumenting if a user ever reports it.

# PART I — FRONTEND ENGINEERING

## Executive Frontend Assessment

Luma's frontend is **architecturally thin and honestly scoped**, with a genuinely good Rust-side sanitization boundary and a disciplined typed IPC client. It is *not* the weak half of the product — but it is **structurally under-designed in exactly two places**: navigation/view-state ownership, and design-token ownership. Both are the kind of debt that grows super-linearly with each new screen, and both are cheap to fix now and expensive to fix later.

Three properties hold today:

- **Server state is never duplicated into a client store.** All data comes from IPC; there is no shadow cache to invalidate. This is a real, rare strength.
- **Durable state ownership is correct and documented** (`SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md`): SQLite owns knowledge, Zustand owns transient reader presentation, `localStorage` owns only the theme.
- **Failures are silent.** Reader load failure = blank viewport + `console.error`. Any render error = white window forever. There is no error boundary, no error surface, and no error telemetry anywhere in the app. This is the single most consequential frontend gap.

**Verdict**: surface-level quality is good, structural quality is mid. No rewrite is warranted. Recommendation: adopt **no new frontend technology** — the fixes are ownership and configuration changes, not architecture swaps.

## Architecture Model

| Dimension | Actual state |
|---|---|
| Organization | Feature-first folders in the app (`features/{library,reader,annotations,workspace,settings,devices,plugins,palette,intelligence}`) + type-based `state/`, `lib/` |
| Package strategy | 6 workspace packages, consumed via public entry points and **lint-enforced** (`no-restricted-imports` bans `@luma/*/src**`) |
| Routing | **None.** `App.tsx` is a two-branch ternary (`currentBook ? Reader : Library`); every other view is switched by `LibraryView`'s `currentSection` local state |
| State | Zustand (1 store, reader only) + ~30 component-local `useState` in `LibraryView` + 10 components calling the module-global `LumaApi` directly |
| Rendering | CSR only, single bundle, no lazy routes, no SSR/SSG (correct for a desktop shell) |
| Styling | Tailwind 3 utility-first + ~40 global `!important` overrides in `styles/index.css` + 135 distinct inline hex literals |
| Design tokens | **Three competing sources** (see [FE-HIGH-2](#-fe-high-2--theme-state-has-three-writers-and-design-tokens-have-three-sources)) |

**Cohesion/coupling verdict**: crates are clean and enforced; packages are clean; the app layer is where cohesion collapses — not by file size alone, but because `LibraryView` owns navigation, filtering, import, selection, analytics, keyboard shortcuts, and 6 modals simultaneously, and because its lifetime is shorter than the state it owns.

## Project Structure

Verified observations:

- Feature folders are real, not decorative — `features/reader/*` contains 9 format/annotation modules, `features/library/*` contains 11.
- **Two divergent copies of one verification harness** exist and disagree (`scripts/verify-epub-highlight.ts` 8,798 B; `apps/desktop/scripts/verify-epub-highlight.ts` 8,162 B), and **neither is wired to any npm script or CI step** (🆕 [FE-MED-4](#-fe-med-4--two-divergent-copies-of-the-epub-verification-harness)).
- `lib/mockData.ts` (435 lines of fixture data) is **statically imported by `lib/tauri.ts`**, so it ships inside the production desktop bundle, and `useMock` defaults to `!isTauri()`.
- No `tailwind.config.js`/`postcss.config.js` surprises: both exist at `apps/desktop/` and are correctly placed.
- `docs/` is unusually rich (43 architecture docs, 24 ADRs, perf harness docs) and is **largely accurate** — except where it describes the stack (see [FE-HIGH-1](#-fe-high-1--documented-stack-does-not-match-the-shipped-stack)).

## Feature Boundaries

Boundaries are structural but **not uniform**:

| Feature | Owns UI | Owns state | Reaches for data via | Testable in isolation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reader | ✅ `features/reader` | ✅ Zustand store via injected context | `useReaderStore` → injected `LumaApiClient` | ✅ yes (DI seam) |
| Library | ✅ `features/library` | ✅ 20+ local `useState` | **`LumaApi` global singleton** | ❌ no |
| Annotations / Workspace / Settings / Devices / Plugins / Palette | ✅ | ✅ | **`LumaApi` global singleton** | ❌ no |

**The DI seam exists but is bypassed by 10 of the ~18 feature components.** `main.tsx` builds a `bootstrapApplication()` transport and passes it into `ReaderStoreProvider`; every non-reader feature ignores it and imports `LumaApi` directly. The project's own testability property therefore holds for the reader only.

Cross-feature issues found:
- `LibraryView` (library feature) imports and routes **6 unrelated features** (annotations, intelligence, workspace ×4, devices, plugins, palette, settings). Feature boundaries exist on disk but are dissolved in the composition root of one god component.
- No cross-feature *state* manipulation found (good — each feature owns its own state).
- No cyclic imports or secret internal imports found; the ESLint boundary rule is real and passes.

## Component Architecture

### 🔴 FE-CRIT-1 — No error boundary, no error surface, no error telemetry

**Current state**: zero matches for `ErrorBoundary`, `componentDidCatch`, `window.onerror`, or `unhandledrejection` in `apps/desktop/src`.
**Evidence**: repo-wide grep (0 hits); `main.tsx` mounts a bare `ReactDOM.createRoot(...).render(<App/>)`.
**Problem**: React 18 unmounts the entire tree on an uncaught render error. In a desktop window that yields a **white, permanently dead window** with no message, no recovery, and (because there is no reporter) no signal that it happened.
**Compounding evidence**: reader load paths swallow failures — `readerState.ts:loadChapter/loadPdfPage/searchInDoc` and `LibraryView.tsx` catch → `logger.error` only. A failed chapter fetch renders an **empty viewport indistinguishable from "still loading"**, which is precisely the "loading = blank screen" and "empty = error" collapse the project's own principles forbid.
**User impact**: HIGH — silent data-absence in the reader; catastrophic loss of the whole UI on any render exception.
**Root cause**: no error-handling layer was ever designed for the UI tier; errors are handled only at the Rust boundary.
**Recommended direction**: (1) one root `ErrorBoundary` + one per-route boundary rendering a recoverable "reload view / return to library" state; (2) convert reader load failures into an explicit `status: 'idle'|'loading'|'ready'|'error'` on the store (the store already has `loading` + `statusMessage`, it simply is not used as a discriminated state); (3) route JS errors + unhandled rejections into the existing `perfTelemetry` sink.
**Complexity**: Low. **Validation**: component test asserting an error in a child renders the fallback; manual fault injection via a mocked rejected IPC call. **Priority**: 🔴 **Do now.** **Owner**: frontend.

### Component granularity

**Too large (evidence-backed):**

| Component | Size | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| `features/library/LibraryView.tsx` | 1,088 lines, **47 hooks**, ~25 `useState`, 6 modals, 20 cross-feature imports | navigation + filtering + import + selection + analytics + keyboard, one lifetime |
| `features/workspace/ResearchProjectWorkspace.tsx` | 832 lines | single-view CRUD screen and its data layer in one component |
| `lib/tauri.ts` | 1,636 lines, **109 methods** | transport + mock backend + localStorage fallback + domain API |
| `features/reader/highlightEngine.ts` | 717 lines | cohesive (one real algorithm) — **not** flagged |
| `crates/luma-reader/src/epub_doc.rs` | 844 lines | cohesive (one format) — **not** flagged |

**Too small / dead weight found (speculative generality):**
- `LibraryViewLabels` (~20 keys) + `LibraryViewConfig` (**17 boolean `enable*` flags**) + a `components` override prop + `className`/`style`: **no caller anywhere sets any of them.** `App.tsx` passes only `isDarkMode` and `onToggleDarkMode`. Every default is `true`, so the flags are unreachable-by-default dead configuration that must be mentally evaluated on every read.
- `packages/design-system`'s `LUMA_THEMES` is exported and **never imported** (verified: only `ANNOTATION_HIGHLIGHT_COLORS` is consumed, in one file).

*Rule applied*: extraction is recommended only where it buys readability/testability, never to hit a line count. `highlightEngine.rs`-style cohesion is left alone.

## Component APIs

Findings on the smallest-public-API principle:

- **`LibraryView` has the largest and least stable public API in the app** (3 required-ish props + 6 optional groups, none of which any consumer exercises). Recommend deletion of `config.sections` / `enable*` flags / `components` and a props surface of `{ isDarkMode, onToggleDarkMode }` until a real second consumer appears.
- **`BookTable` (packages/library-ui) accepts `onOpenDetails` and silently ignores it** (`onOpenDetails: _onOpenDetails`). `LibraryView` passes it. Result: in list view, the row-click and the details affordance are dead — a **silent capability gap** introduced by a prop that lies.
- **`BookCard` uses a clickable `<div onClick>` as its root**; wrapping it in `role="button"` would require composing around the nested `<button>` (invalid nesting). Needs a real composition pass (root = `<button>` or `role="button"` + `<span>` actions).
- `Button` (packages/ui) is the good pattern: native `<button>`, `...props` forwarding, `variant`/`size` unions instead of boolean explosion. It is the model the rest should follow.
- **`deleteBookPermanently(bookId, deleteFiles: boolean)`** — a boolean flag parameter where the app has exactly one call site and passes `false` unconditionally. Control coupling with a single possible value.
- Ref forwarding: absent everywhere, including `Button`/`Badge`. Acceptable today (no consumer needs it); document rather than add speculatively.

## State Inventory & Ownership

| State | Class | Owner (actual) | Correct owner? |
|---|---|---|---|
| books, collections, tags, authors, analytics | Server/Remote | `LibraryView` local `useState` | ⚠️ lifespan tied to a component that can unmount mid-session |
| `authors` + `globalAnnotations` (annotations feature) | Server/Remote | §2 of `LibraryView` | ⚠️ same |
| `currentSection`, `searchQuery`, `formatFilter`, `statusFilter`, `sortBy`, `viewMode`, `currentPage`, `selectedCollectionId`, `selectedTagId` | Navigation + UI filter | `LibraryView` local | ❌ [FE-HIGH-3](#-fe-high-3--navigation-state-is-owned-by-a-component-with-a-shorter-lifetime-than-the-state) |
| `isCommandPaletteOpen`, `isSettingsOpen`, 4 modal flags, `isDragging` | Local UI | `LibraryView` local | ✅ |
| reader session: `documentData`, `annotations`, `bookmarks`, `readingProgress`, `activeSessionId` | Server/Remote + session | Zustand store | ✅ mostly (see ARCH-MED-2 for the progress-flush gap) |
| `sidebarTab`, `isTypographyOpen`, `searchQuery`, `searchResults`, `statusMessage`, `pendingScrollLocator` | Local UI / ephemeral | Zustand store | ❌ **global store used for local UI concerns** (only the reader renders; these never cross features) |
| `settings.theme` (reader) | Persisted preference | Zustand **and** `App` `useState` **and** DOM class **and** `localStorage` **and** `DEFAULT_READER_SETTINGS.theme="dark"` | ❌ four writers, three sources |
| `isDarkMode` (app chrome) | Persisted preference | `App` local `useState` + `localStorage["luma_theme"]` | ❌ duplicates the above |
| `isFullscreen` | Local UI | `ReaderView` local | ✅ |
| import modal: 20+ interacting booleans | Multi-step async workflow | `LibraryView` local | ⚠️ candidate for an explicit state machine (see below) |

### 🔴 FE-HIGH-2 — Theme state has three writers and design tokens have three sources

**Evidence**
- `App.tsx:50-60` — `useState` seeded from `localStorage.getItem("luma_theme")`, writes DOM class + `colorScheme` + `localStorage` on change.
- `state/readerState.ts` `updateSettings()` — **independently** toggles `document.documentElement.classList` and writes the *same* `localStorage` key.
- `readerState.ts` initial `settings.theme` reads the same key again; `ReaderView` resolves `isDarkMode = propsDarkMode ?? settings.theme === "dark"` — so `readerState.settings.theme` and `App.isDarkMode` are two copies of one truth that are only reconciled by both happening to write the same string.
- `DEFAULT_READER_SETTINGS.theme` is `"dark"` while the app defaults to light (`localStorage` absent ⇒ `false`).
- **Token sources**: `design-system` (`LUMA_THEMES`, unused, and its `dark.bg #18181B` ≠ `App`'s `dark:bg-[#141312]`), `styles/index.css` (`:root`/`.dark` custom properties, values differ again), `reader-ui` `READER_THEME_STYLES` (`bg-slate-950` — a *blue*-black, visibly off-system), and **135 distinct inline hex literals** across 30+ components (top offenders: `ResearchProjectWorkspace` 165, `ReaderSidebar` 126, `SettingsModal` 123).

**Problem**: theme is not a single source of truth, and there is no token to change when a colour changes. `#141312`, `#18181B`, `#FAF7F2` and `slate-950` are all "the app background" in dark/light depending on where you look.
**Impact**: correctness (desync is possible by construction), maintainability (a rebrand touches 4 layers + 135 literals), accessibility (contrast cannot be audited centrally).
**Recommended direction**: one owner — a `theme` slice in a store (or a `ThemeProvider`), persisting through the **settings IPC/SQLite path** rather than `localStorage` (the project's own zero-durable-localStorage invariant already names theme as the sole exception; keeping it consistent is still cheaper than a second path), and exactly one token layer (`design-system` → CSS custom properties in `index.css`); delete `LUMA_THEMES` or make it the generator of the CSS variables.
**Complexity**: Medium (mechanical). **Validation**: a test asserting one writer; visual diff of light/dark; contrast audit script over the token set. **Priority**: 🔴 HIGH.

### FE-HIGH-3 — Navigation state is owned by a component with a shorter lifetime than the state

**Evidence**: `App.tsx` renders `currentBook ? <ReaderView/> : <LibraryView/>`. All navigation/filter state lives inside `LibraryView`. Opening a book unmounts `LibraryView`; returning remounts it fresh.
**Impact**: returning from a book **discards the current section, search query, format/status filters, sort order, page, and any open panel**. There is no URL, no history, no restore. This is a data-ownership defect, not a styling issue: the state outlives nothing.
**Recommended direction**: (a) move navigation/filter state into a `viewState` store slice or context above the route branch so it survives the reader; (b) if deep-linking/restore is wanted, make it URL/route-shaped (a desktop app can still use the hash router — it costs nothing and buys restore + shareable state); (c) do **not** lift all 20 booleans — only the ones that must survive.
**Complexity**: Medium. **Validation**: open a book from a filtered grid → return → assert the filter is intact. **Priority**: 🟠 HIGH.

### FE-MED-1 — Global store holding local UI state

`sidebarTab`, `isTypographyOpen`, `pendingScrollLocator`, `searchQuery`/`searchResults` in the reader store are read by exactly one subtree. They are in the store because the store was the convenient place, not because they are cross-feature. `pendingScrollLocator` exists *only* to bridge a store action to a DOM effect (see FE-MED-5). Recommend keeping the store for session data and deriving UI toggles locally (or accepting them explicitly as a documented "reader UI" slice) — but decide the rule, because the current split has no criterion.

### State machines — where justified

The library import flow carries ~20 interacting booleans/flags (`isImportModalOpen`, `activeImportJob`, `isDuplicateModalOpen`, `duplicateExistingBook`, `duplicateImportingFile`, `isDragging`, …) plus job-progress events. Impossible/contradictory combinations are representable (e.g. duplicate modal open with a null `duplicateExistingBook` — the code defensively checks before use). A discriminated union (`idle | importing{job} | duplicate{existing,file} | done | error`) would make those states unrepresentable. **Justified** for import + duplicate review; **not** justified for the reader's toggles.

## Server vs Client State

**Verified strong**: no server data is mirrored into Zustand/Redux. No cache staleness is possible because there is no cache.
**Cost of that choice (verified)**: no dedup/invalidation either.
- `LibraryView` refetches `books`+`collections`+`tags`+`authors` on mount and again after **every** mutation (`createHighlight` → `saveAnnotation` then `listAnnotations`; every tag/status/trash/restore action → `loadData()` + `handleOpenDetails()`).
- Reader annotation mutations always re-list the full annotation set (`createHighlight`, `deleteAnnotation`, `updateAnnotationNote`) instead of updating locally from the response.
**Impact**: unnecessary IPC chatter and a visible refetch flash on every small edit; no correctness bug. **Direction**: mutate the returned entity into local state; keep a full refetch only for import/reconcile. **Priority**: 🟡 Medium (perf/UX, not correctness).

## URL State

Not applicable as a *web* concern (desktop shell, no shareable URLs, no SEO requirement — see FE-N/A-1). But the **behavioral** part of URL state — "can the user get back to where they were, and can that state be described?" — is missing (FE-HIGH-3). Treat this as **navigation-state ownership**, not as a routing-framework request.

## Data Fetching

- Fetching is colocated with the UI that displays it (no central fetch layer) — acceptable at this size, and it is why there is no duplicated server state.
- Cancellation: **none**. `loadChapter`/`loadPdfPage`/`loadBooks` have no `AbortSignal` and no stale-response guard. Rapid arrow-key page turns in the reader can resolve out of order and set an older page's data. This is a concrete race introduced by the keyboard-repeat path in `ReaderView`.
- Retries: none (and none needed for local IPC, though a failed file read deserves one user-visible retry).
- Loading states: `loading` boolean only; no distinct "retrying"/"stale" representation.

## Caching

Deliberately and correctly absent on the client (browser/HTTP cache is irrelevant for IPC; Rust owns LRU caching of canonical documents). Recommendation: **do not** add a client server-state library. There is no duplicate-fetch *correctness* problem, only redundant IPC on mutations, which local state updates fix without a new dependency.

## Loading / Error / Empty / Partial States

| Surface | loading | empty | error | partial | retry |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Library grid | ✅ distinct | ✅ distinct ("no books match") | ✅ single error banner + retry | ❌ (a failed tags fetch silently yields `{}` via `.catch`) | ✅ |
| Reader chapter/page | ⚠️ `loading` flag exists but the viewport renders blank either way | ❌ no "empty chapter" state | ❌ **console-only** | ❌ | ❌ |
| Annotation center | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ unhandled (`Promise.all` → `.catch(() => [])`) | ❌ | ❌ |
| Import | ✅ progress modal | n/a | ❌ job failure surfaces as a status message only | ✅ duplicate path is explicit | ❌ |
| Settings/backup/maintenance | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ status strings | ❌ | ✅ |

The library tier is the model to copy; the reader tier is where the anti-pattern lives.

## Rendering Strategy / Server-Client Boundaries / Hydration

- **CSR-only, correctly chosen** for a desktop shell. No SSR/SSG/ISR/RSC/islands — and no requirement justifies them. **Explicitly not-justified change**: do not introduce a meta-framework here.
- Hydration: N/A (no SSR). No hydration mismatch class of bug exists.
- Server/client boundary is the IPC surface (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/*`, 16 modules) — reviewed in PART III.

## Performance

Measured during this audit:

| Metric | Value | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Initial JS (single chunk) | **948.5 kB min / 266.6 kB gzip** | Large for an offline desktop shell |
| CSS | **246.3 kB min / 49.6 kB gzip** | Large; driven by 135 inline palettes + 40 `!important` overrides |
| Worker (lazy, correct) | 2,228 kB `pdf.worker` | Acceptable — separate file, not initial JS |
| Route/feature code splitting | **none** | 🔴 HIGH (see below) |
| Lazy imports in src | 3, all `@tauri-apps/api/*` | pdfjs, all feature views, mock data are eager |

### 🟠 FE-HIGH-4 — No code splitting; everything is in one eager chunk

**Evidence**: `vite.config.ts` has no `build.rollupOptions`/`manualChunks`; the only dynamic imports in the app are Tauri API modules; `App.tsx` statically imports `LibraryView` and `ReaderView`; `PdfReaderView` → `pdfWorker.ts` → `import * as pdfjsLib from "pdfjs-dist"` is static.
**Problem**: a user who only browses their library pays for the entire PDF renderer, the archive readers, six workspace screens, the annotation center, the plugin/device centres, the mock data store, **and the 435-line fixture library**. Vite's own build warning fires (`chunks are larger than 500 kB`).
**Impact**: start-to-interactive on cold app launch — the one metric a desktop reader is judged on.
**Recommended direction**: `React.lazy` + `Suspense` for the six non-library screens and each reader engine, keeping `LibraryView` (the landing surface) eager; move `mockData.ts` behind the test/mock entry so it is excluded from the Tauri build entirely (a build-time `import.meta.env` branch, not a runtime `isTauri()` branch). Measure with the existing `perfTelemetry` marks (`LUMA_PERF_REACT_MOUNT`, `LUMA_PERF_READER_VISIBLE`) before/after.
**Complexity**: Low–Medium. **Validation**: chunk report before/after; `LUMA_PERF_*` deltas on a cold launch. **Priority**: 🟠 HIGH.

**Bundle/dependency questions (evidence: no `pnpm audit` findings reported by prior audit; no unused-dependency sweep done here):** `playwright` is declared at root **and** in `apps/desktop` with **no config file and no specs anywhere** → dead dev dependency (remove or wire up E2E). `jsdom` is installed but `vitest.config.ts` sets `environment: "node"` and no test uses it → dead dev dependency.

### Core Web Vitals / LCP / INP / CLS

**Not measurable, and this is a finding in itself.** There is no field/RUM capture (the `perfTelemetry` collector is in-memory, `maxEvents: 1000`, with `flush()` called only by the test bridge binary); no bundle budget in CI; no CI performance gate for the frontend at all (the Rust perf harness is budget-asserted — the frontend has no equivalent). Evidence for CLS-relevant risk: web font loading (see FE-MED-2) with no `size-adjust`/fallback metrics; no image dimensions on cover `<img>` (aspect-ratio box present in `BookCard`, so this one is mitigated).

### FE-MED-2 — The shipped app cannot load its fonts, and it tries to load them from a third party

**Evidence**: `apps/desktop/index.html` declares `preconnect` to `fonts.googleapis.com`/`fonts.gstatic.com` and a stylesheet `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Lora…&family=Playfair+Display…&family=Plus+Jakarta+Sans…">`. `tauri.conf.json` sets CSP `default-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: asset: https:;` with **no `style-src`, no `font-src`** ⇒ both fall back to `default-src 'self'`, which does **not** permit an external stylesheet origin.
**Problem, two-sided**:
1. **Dev/prod divergence**: in `pnpm dev` (no CSP) the fonts load and the UI looks as designed; in the packaged app the stylesheet is blocked and every screen silently falls back to Georgia/system — and since a large share of the design *is* typography (`--reader-font-family: Lora, Georgia, serif`, `.drop-cap` in Playfair Display, `font-serif` throughout), the shipped product looks different from the design.
2. **Product contradiction**: a local-first, offline, "zero cloud dependency, own your data" desktop reader makes a **third-party network request on every launch**. Offline-first apps must not need the network to look right.
**Recommended direction**: self-host the three families as part of the bundle (subset + `font-display: swap` + `woff2`), which removes the network call, removes the CSP conflict, and fixes offline rendering. If self-hosting is rejected, the CSP must be widened to `font-src https://fonts.gstatic.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com` — widening CSP should be the *losing* option here.
**Complexity**: Low. **Validation**: load the packaged app offline and confirm the reader renders in Lora; assert no request to a non-`asset:`/`self` origin. **Priority**: 🟠 HIGH.

### FE-MED-3 — Accessibility of the interaction layer

Measured inventory across `apps/desktop/src`:

- 28 `aria-label`, 6 `role="dialog"`, 6 `aria-modal`, 5 `aria-pressed`, 4 `aria-live`, 3 `onKeyDown`, **4 `tabIndex`** — for a UI with hundreds of interactive elements.
- **14 files contain click handlers and zero accessibility affordances**: all four format readers, `ReaderSidebar`, `TypographySettingsDrawer`, `TextSelectionToolbar`, `SettingsModal`, `CommandPaletteModal`, `KnowledgeHome`, `NotesWorkspace`, `ResearchProjectWorkspace`, `StudyFlashcards`, `IntegrationsPluginsView`. (This is a *conservative* measure — those files have no `aria-*`, no `role=`, no `tabIndex`, no `onKeyDown` at all.)
- Non-semantic interactive elements: `BookCard` root is `<div onClick>`; `BookTable` rows are `<tr onClick>`; `AnnotationItem`'s quote is a `<blockquote onClick>` with no role/tabIndex.
- Icon-only buttons in `ReaderView` carry `title` but no `aria-label` (6 of them) — a name source that is unreliable for AT and shows only on hover.
- `SettingsModal` is an overlay with **no** `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal`, no `Escape` handling, and no focus management (verified by inspecting the file). `CommandPaletteModal` handles `Escape` and autofocuses its input but has **no focus trap and no focus restore**.
- Global `user-select: none` on `body` **and** `select-none` on `<body class=…>` — text cannot be selected anywhere outside the reader content, including error messages, quotes in the annotation list, and metadata values. Copy/paste of a user's own data is broken by default.
- Focus visibility: `packages/ui`'s `Button` sets `focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-stone-400/40` — a 40 %-opacity grey ring on a `#FAF7F2` background is very unlikely to meet the WCAG 2.2 AA 3:1 focus-appearance requirement; the ring is also not `focus-visible`-scoped.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: no usage anywhere (the app uses `animate-pulse`, `animate-in`, smooth scrolling, and a persistent PDF canvas filter).
- Contrast: cannot be audited centrally because colours are scattered across 135 literals; `dark .pdf-canvas-container canvas { filter: invert(.9) hue-rotate(180deg) … }` means PDF content colours are *transformed*, which invalidates any static contrast guarantee for PDFs.

**Impact**: keyboard-only and AT users cannot reliably operate the reader toolbar, the settings dialog, or the library grid; a11y regressions are undetectable because there are no component tests.
**Recommended direction**: (1) make dialog a real component (`<dialog>` or `role="dialog"` + trap + restore + `Escape`) and use it for all 6 modals; (2) fix the four non-semantic click surfaces to real buttons/links; (3) `body { user-select: text }` with `select-none` applied narrowly to chrome; (4) visible `focus-visible` ring from a token; (5) add `prefers-reduced-motion` guards; (6) adopt a rule that any new interactive element ships with its accessible name and keyboard path.
**Complexity**: Medium (mechanical, high value). **Validation**: `vitest` + Testing Library keyboard tests once the harness exists; manual keyboard-only pass of "open book → turn page → highlight → add note → return to library". **Priority**: 🟠 HIGH. **Owner**: frontend.

## Assets

- Images: cover thumbnails use `loading="lazy"` and a fixed `aspect-[3/4.2]` box (CLS-safe), `alt={displayTitle}` present — **good**.
- Fonts: as above (external CDN, blocked by CSP, no `font-display`/subsetting strategy in the repo).
- No `srcset`/`sizes` anywhere: covers are rendered at intrinsic size from `cover_image_path` (a data/asset URL). For a local file this is mostly a decode-memory cost on large scans; low priority.
- PDF: rendered lazily per page with an intersection gate (`PdfPageCanvas`, with an explanatory comment) — **good and documented**.

## Render Performance

- No virtualization on the library grid, and pagination is fake (FE-MED-4) ⇒ **all matching books are in the DOM at once**. For a 1,000-book library this is 1,000 cover cards + images. This is the frontend's most likely INP/layout hotspot, and it is reachable with ordinary use.
- Memoization: `useCallback`/`useMemo` are used heavily in `LibraryView` (part of the 47-hook count) **before** any profiling evidence. Per the project's own principle (and this auditor's), memoization should follow a profile. Recommend: profile a 1,000-book library first, then fix the real cause (pagination/virtualization), and delete the `useCallback`s that don't affect a measured render.
- The reader re-applies DOM highlights on every annotation/search change by rewriting `<mark>` nodes in the chapter subtree (`applyHighlightsAndSearch` + `clearDomHighlights`), i.e. full re-marking rather than diffing. Correct and simple; watch it with large annotation counts (a `MutationObserver`-free design keeps it predictable — a reasonable trade).

### 🟠 FE-MED-4 — Library pagination is decorative and the UI states false values

**Evidence** (`features/library/LibraryView.tsx` + `packages/library-ui`):
- `const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1)` is **never used to slice or filter `books`** (only passed to `<Pagination>`); the grid renders `books.map(...)` in full.
- `<Pagination>` is hardcoded to buttons **1, 2, 3, …, 12** with `onPageChange(12)` literal and `totalPages = 12` default, ignoring the real `totalPages` prop except for the Next/Previous clamp.
- The footer label is `labels.showingItemsLabel(1, books.length, books.length)` — literally "Showing 1-N of N" regardless of state.
**Impact**: the pager is a control that does nothing meaningful (clicks change a number that affects nothing); with the hardcoded 12 the user is invited to page through a library that never pages. This is a user-facing falsehood, not a styling nit.
**Direction**: either implement real paging (slice + stable sort + page reset on filter change) or remove the pager and rely on scroll + virtualization. Do not ship a third state.
**Complexity**: Low. **Priority**: 🟠 HIGH (correctness/UX). **Validation**: a component test asserting page 2 renders items 21-40.

### FE-MED-5 — Hidden coupling: a stringly-typed `window` event bus

`readerState.ts` bridges store actions to DOM effects via `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("luma-reader-scroll-to", {detail:{locator}}))` with emitters at 4 sites and a listener in `EpubReaderView`, plus a `pendingScrollLocator` field whose only purpose is to carry state across that hop. Verified still open from the prior registry (CQ-07).
**Impact**: the contract is invisible to the type system and to any reader of either file; a typo or a renamed event fails silently (no listener ⇒ no scroll, no error). **Direction**: keep the scroll intent as store state and consume it with an effect (the `pendingScrollLocator` field already exists), or export a single typed event map. Do not introduce a global event bus.

### FE-MED-6 — Debug tracing left in production paths

`console.log("[LUMA-OPEN] …")` step traces (1→11) remain in `App.tsx`, `readerState.ts` (5 sites), `LibraryView.tsx` (4 sites), `EpubReaderView.tsx` (2 sites), plus `console.error`/`console.warn` for real errors. The app already has a logger abstraction (`LumaApiConfig.logger`, `ReaderStoreConfig.logger`) which these calls bypass.
**Impact**: noisy console in shipped builds, JSON payloads with timestamps logged per navigation, and genuine errors buried among them. **Direction**: delete the tracing, or move it behind the existing logger at `debug` level. **Priority**: 🔵 Low (trivial).

### FE-MED-7 — Command palette can open the wrong book

`LibraryView.tsx`: `const b = books.find((x) => x.id === id) || books[0]; if (b) setCurrentBook(b);` — when the action targets a book not present in the currently loaded/filtered `books` array, the app **opens the first book in the list**. Wrong-document navigation from a search result is exactly the class of bug this project's "annotation integrity" ethos is about. **Direction**: fail loudly (status message) or fetch the book by id. **Priority**: 🟡 Medium.

### FE-N/A-1 — SEO (correctly not attempted)

A local-first desktop reader behind IPC has no crawlability requirement. No metadata/canonical/structured-data work is warranted. **Explicitly not-justified change.**

### FE-CTX-1 — i18n (contextual)

~135 hardcoded UI strings; a hand-rolled label-injection surface exists **only** in `LibraryView` (~20 keys, never overridden by a caller); `toLocaleDateString("en-US", …)` is hardcoded; no pluralization/RTL/text-expansion strategy. For a single-locale desktop app this is **fine and should not be changed now** — but the half-built `labels` surface is worse than either alternative: it implies internationalization without delivering it and inflates the largest component's API. Recommendation: delete `LibraryViewLabels` now; if i18n is ever a product requirement, adopt a real solution and retrofit all screens at once.

### FE-CTX-2 — Analytics / observability / privacy

No analytics SDK, no RUM, no error reporting (see FE-CRIT-1). What exists is `perfTelemetry` (in-memory ring buffer, dev console output only, exported by the test bridge). Nothing captures passwords/tokens — **there is nothing to capture**, which is the correct state. The gap is *diagnosis*: if a user reports "highlights flicker", there is no data path to confirm it.

### FE-CTX-3 — Browser compatibility / progressive enhancement

No `browserslist`, no polyfills, `build.target: "esnext"` — correct for a WebView2/WebKit-bound desktop shell (a fixed, modern engine). Feature detection is used where it matters (`isTauri()`, `typeof window !== "undefined"`, `typeof localStorage !== "undefined"`). **No change recommended.**

---

# PART II — CODE QUALITY & MAINTAINABILITY

## Executive Code Quality Assessment

The codebase is **unusually well-behaved for its size** and shows real discipline: strict TypeScript with zero `any` (the prior audit's CQ-10 is **fixed**), ESLint clean with a genuine architecture-boundary rule, Rust clippy-zero, typed domain errors, and a Rust architecture fitness test that now **actually runs and passes** (prior CQ-08 **fixed**). Comments are why-oriented and often excellent (`luma-security/src/lib.rs` explains its sanitizer trade-offs in ~40 lines of rationale — model behaviour).

Debt is **not diffuse**; it is concentrated in four places: the test suite's side effects (new), `lib/tauri.ts`, `LibraryView.tsx`, and the CSS/theme layer. One new 🆕 finding is a genuine process hazard (§CQ-CRIT-1).

## Project Maturity

**Growing Product**, knocking on Production. Markers present: workspace tooling, 3-OS CI, strict linters, `deny.toml`, architecture fitness tests, 53 frontend + ~40 Rust test files, budget-asserted Rust perf harness. Markers absent: any UI error handling/observability, any frontend component/behavior test tier, any bundle budget, hermetic tests, and honest docs about the shipped stack. **Do not add enterprise ceremony** — the gaps above are the ones that matter at this maturity.

## Architecture Map & Dependency Direction

Verified from manifests and enforced by `crates/luma-storage/tests/architecture_boundaries.rs` (**passing**):

```text
luma-core ← luma-security, luma-anchor, luma-sync, luma-ai
luma-reader ← luma-core, luma-security
luma-storage ← luma-core, luma-anchor, luma-reader, luma-security
luma-search ← luma-core, luma-storage
desktop app ← (IPC over the Tauri boundary)
```

Acyclic, stable-direction, no upward dependency, and — new since the prior audit — **a test that fails if a new crate or edge escapes the policy**, including the clever `layering_table_covers_every_workspace_crate` guard. This is the strongest single quality artefact in the repository. **Preserve.**

Frontend dependency direction: app → `@luma/*` public entry points only (lint-enforced). Packages do not import the app. Clean.

Weak edges: `luma-sync` (68 LOC) and `luma-ai` (172 LOC) still have **zero non-root dependents** (contextual debt; the fitness table now documents them as intended-but-unused, which is an honest improvement).

## Cohesion

- **High**: crate boundaries; `luma-reader`'s one-format-per-module design; `highlightEngine.ts`; `PdfPageCanvas.tsx`; `Button`/`Badge` in `packages/ui`.
- **Low**: `LibraryView` (≥6 reasons to change), `lib/tauri.ts` (transport + mock + fallback persistence + 109 domain methods), `readerState.ts` (session lifecycle + progress persistence + annotation CRUD + bookmarks + search + UI toggles + theme side effects + format-specific navigation), `styles/index.css` (tokens + resets + prose typography + highlight styles + PDF.js overrides + Tailwind-fighting overrides in one file).

## Coupling

Detected, with evidence:
- **Hidden coupling**: the `window` CustomEvent bus (FE-MED-5); `perfTelemetry` as a module-level singleton captured at import time in the store factory (injectable — but the default binds the global, so tests must remember to override it); `LumaApi` module-global singleton reached by 10 components.
- **Common mutable state**: the mock store inside `LumaApiClient` (mutated by `createNote`/`createFlashcard`/etc. in mock mode).
- **Control coupling**: `deleteBookPermanently(id, deleteFiles)`; `LibraryViewConfig.enable*` flags (unreachable); `_call(cmd, args, mockFn)` — a 3-arg private helper that every one of 109 methods must route through with a mock branch.
- **Stamp coupling (accepted)**: `Database`/`CacheManager`/services are `Clone`-cheap `Arc` handles passed freely in Rust — appropriate and documented.
- **Explicit, parameter-based coupling** dominates overall — the audit did **not** find "coupling for the sake of metrics" nor abstraction layers created to flatter a graph.

## Public / Internal Boundaries

- Rust: `pub` is liberal but the only consumer is the workspace; low risk today.
- `packages/*`: public entry points enforced by lint. ✅
- **Missing**: the desktop app's *own* internal boundaries are unenforced — nothing prevents `features/workspace/*` from importing `features/reader/*` internals. As the feature count grows (it went from 3 to 10 features), this is the boundary most likely to rot. A single additional `no-restricted-imports` rule (features may import `features/<x>/index.ts` only) would be proportionately valuable.

## Readability / Naming

Strong. Domain vocabulary is consistent and correct (`spine`, `anchor`, `canonical`, `reflowable`, `locator`, `BookFile`). Test names are scenario-descriptive. **Counter-examples found**: `atrium` and `history` as sidebar section names with no domain meaning defined anywhere; `luma_*` floating `localStorage` keys; `LUMA-OPEN` step numbers 1→11 whose missing steps (5.5?) make the trace read as machine-generated; `_onOpenDetails` (an ignored parameter that names a promise the code does not keep).

## Comments

Valuable: `luma-security`'s sanitizer rationale and its "trade-off" note; `PdfPageCanvas`'s intersection-gating rationale; `strip_raw_html_blocks`'s explicit contract trade-off; `MockDataStore`'s inline comment that `SanitizerConfig` "is no longer used by `sanitize_untrusted_html`" (honest, prevents a wrong-suspicion hunt).
No lying comments, no restating-the-code comments, no stale-TODO plague found in sampled files. **This is a strength to keep.**

## Functions / Methods

No pathological long functions in Rust. `LibraryView`'s render is one ~400-line JSX expression tree with three branches (home/empty/grid) built inside a `useCallback` with a 20-entry dependency array — the frontend's clearest accidental-complexity site. Not a "line count" complaint: the same block mixes data shaping, telemetry, navigation, and presentation.

## Classes / Modules

| Module | Size | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/tauri.ts` | 1,636 L / 109 methods | **God module, still open (CQ-01)** — every new IPC command edits this file twice (method + mock branch) + `shared-types` + the Rust command module |
| `features/library/LibraryView.tsx` | 1,088 L / 47 hooks | **God component, still open (CQ-03)** |
| `state/readerState.ts` | 679 L | Large but *partially* cohesive; three concerns are separable (server/session data, UI toggles, navigation) |
| `crates/luma-storage/src/repos/knowledge_repo.rs` | 789 L | Cohesive (one domain) — **not** flagged |
| `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/bin/browser_reader_bridge.rs` | 294 L | Test-only binary in the shipped crate tree (see ARCH-MED-4) |
| `lib/mockData.ts` | 435 L | Fixture data in the production source tree and bundle |

## Complexity

Essential complexity (EPUB/PDF/CBZ parsing, fuzzy anchoring, migrations, text-layer geometry) is **localized and correctly kept**; that is the right trade and should not be "simplified". Accidental complexity: (a) the transport/mock/fallback duality threaded through 109 methods; (b) the 47-hook component; (c) three theme systems; (d) CSS that overrides generated utilities; (e) a `.catch(() => [])` on a real data fetch that converts failure into empty.

## Code Smells (evidence-backed)

1. **Bloater — God module**: `tauri.ts` (109 methods, dual responsibility). *Divergent change.*
2. **Bloater — God component**: `LibraryView.tsx`. *Divergent change.*
3. **Dispensable — Speculative generality**: `LibraryViewConfig.sections` (17 flags) + `LibraryViewLabels` (20 keys) + `components` prop, no caller; `LUMA_THEMES` exported-never-imported; `sanitize_untrusted_html_with_config` + `SanitizerConfig` used only by their own tests (documented); `luma-sync`/`luma-ai` (still zero dependents).
4. **Dispensable — Dead code / dead capability**: `BookTable.onOpenDetails` accepted and ignored; `Pagination.currentPage` state with no effect; `playwright`+`jsdom` dev deps unused.
5. **Coupler — Hidden dependency**: `window` CustomEvent bus + module-global `LumaApi`.
6. **Modern smell — Lying UI**: `BookTable` fabricates `35%` progress and derives status badges from that fabricated number; guesses format by substring-matching the *file id* (`file_id.includes("pdf")`), which is a domain primitive read by string search.
7. **Modern smell — Utility dumping ground (borderline)**: `tauri.ts` also carries `isTauri`, `MockDataStore`, `ConsoleLogger`, label defaults, and a legacy-migration routine.
8. **Duplicated knowledge**: per-format `ReadingProgress` construction repeated 4× in `readerState.ts` (identical `book_id/progress/locator/title/page/total/last_read_at/sync` shape with only the locator differing) — this *is* change-together knowledge (any new `ReadingProgress` field must be added in 4 places); the fan-out progress computation and persisted progress are separate code paths that must agree.
9. **Duplicated knowledge**: two divergent `verify-epub-highlight.ts` copies (FE-MED-4 / CQ-MED-2).
10. **Primitive obsession (minor)**: `current_locator` is a stringly-typed, per-format mini-language (`epubcfi(/6/4!/4/1:0)`, `page=12`, `offset:120`, `md:offset=120`, raw integer) parsed by **regex in five places** across `readerState.ts`, `EpubReaderView.tsx` and the Rust side. This is one concept (`DocumentPosition`) reimplemented as string matching repeatedly — the highest-value *abstraction* candidate in the frontend. Not a defect today; it is precisely the kind of duplicated knowledge that becomes one.
11. **No smell found (worth stating)**: no cargo-cult SOLID, no interface-per-class, no DI ceremony, no deep inheritance, no magic-number plague, no lying comments.

## Abstractions

| Abstraction | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `LumaTransport` / `LumaApiConfig.invoke` injection | ✅ **Justified** — two real implementations (Tauri, browser bridge) + full test suite runs without Tauri |
| `ReaderStoreProvider` DI context | ✅ **Justified** but **bypassed by 10 components** (see ARCH-MED-1) — the abstraction is right, the adoption is half-done |
| `_call(cmd, args, mockFn)` mock-branch pattern | ⚠️ **Right idea, wrong shape** — 109 call sites each carrying a mock closure inline; a mock *transport* (`MockTransport implements LumaTransport`) would delete every branch and shrink the file by hundreds of lines while keeping the same tests green |
| `sanitize_untrusted_html_with_config`/`SanitizerConfig` | ❌ Dead public API (documented as such) — delete or use |
| `luma-ai` traits | ⚠️ Premature (zero implementations consumed) — keep frozen, revisit on a real trigger |
| `LUMA_THEMES` | ❌ Dead; also the *wrong* abstraction for a CSS-variable-based theme system |
| `highlightEngine` | ✅ Justified — one algorithm, five consumers (reader views, tests, verifier script), replaced a genuinely hard problem |

## Duplication

- **Fix (knowledge duplication)**: `ReadingProgress` construction ×4; the two verification scripts; `BookTable`'s format/progress heuristics duplicating knowledge that already exists in the domain model.
- **Leave (incidental)**: the six document engines share a structural shape but encode different format knowledge — deduplicating them would create a wrong abstraction, and this auditor explicitly recommends **not** doing it.
- **Leave (intentional)**: per-package `tsconfig.json` files (each with its own intent), crate-level test helpers.

## SOLID

Applied with restraint. SRP violated exactly where flagged (god module, god component, reader store). OCP/LSP/ISP: no violations found — no hierarchies to violate, no speculative interface sets, consumers are concrete. DIP: used only where it pays (`LumaTransport`, store DI) — **not** applied to Rust services that have one implementation, which is the correct call. No refactor is warranted to "improve SOLID" here.

## Composition / Inheritance

Rust: composition only. TS: hooks + prop composition; no HOCs, no inheritance anywhere. `BookCard`'s nested-interactive-element problem (clickable div wrapping a button) is a **composition design gap**, and fixing it is the one component-API change worth making.

## Error Handling

| Layer | State |
|---|---|
| Rust services/repos | ✅ Typed `LumaError`, `map_err` discipline, clippy-clean |
| Tauri commands | ✅ Good — panics in `commands/*` are essentially absent (all 17 `unwrap`/`expect` hits are the **test-only bridge binary**, plus 2 boot-time expects in `context.rs` and 1 in `main.rs::run`, both appropriate) |
| `_call` (TS boundary) | ⚠️ Logs then rethrows the raw error — typed Rust errors arrive as strings; the type information is lost at exactly the boundary where the UI would need it |
| Feature components | ❌ `catch (e) { console.error(…) }` and `.catch(() => [])` — failures become empty data or silence |
| UI presentation of failure | ❌ one string `statusMessage`; no error types, no retry semantics per operation |

**Direction**: keep Rust as-is; give the TS client an error normalizer producing `{ kind: 'notFound'|'io'|'conflict'|'unknown', message }` so features can branch on *meaning* rather than string, and give each async surface a state enum. **Priority**: 🟡 Medium (but do it together with FE-CRIT-1).

## State / Side Effects

- Zustand state is explicit and owned ✅.
- `readerState.updateSettings` performing DOM + `localStorage` side effects inside a store action ❌ (store actions should return state; the theme writer belongs to one owner).
- Module-level singletons: `LumaApi`, `perfTelemetry`, `defaultReaderStore` — acceptable in a single-window app, documented, with reset hooks for tests ✅ (with the caveat that components bypass them, ARCH-MED-1).
- Debounced progress persistence holds a closure-scoped `setTimeout` **outside** the store (`progressDebounceTimer` in the factory) — invisible to the store's state machine and untestable without fake timers. It is also where the flush-on-close bug lives (ARCH-MED-2).

## Concurrency

- Rust: `RwLock` session caches with bounded inserts; dual read/write connections; concurrency fitness suite passes. Sound.
- TS: the meaningful concurrency is **IPC races**, not threads: no cancellation or stale-response guards in `loadChapter`/`loadPdfPage`/`loadBooks` (see Data Fetching). Rapid page-turning can commit an out-of-order response. **Recommendation**: a request-sequence guard in the store (`const seq = ++this.loadSeq; if (seq !== this.loadSeq) return;`) — a few lines, removes a real class of glitch.

## Testability

**Verified numbers**: 53 frontend tests across 9 files, all harness/state level (`it`/`test` count 55 including 2 skipped-style); 34 Rust test files including a concurrency fitness suite and budget-asserted perf harness.

**The gap is the missing tier**: no `@testing-library/react`, no `user-event`, `vitest.config.ts` uses `environment: "node"` while `jsdom` sits unused in devDependencies, and no component renders in any test. Consequences (all evidence-backed): the 47-hook component has no behavioral coverage; accessibility cannot regress-detect; `BookCard`'s keyboard unusability and the fake pagination are both invisible to CI; the tree is not checked for error resilience (FE-CRIT-1).
**Direction**: add Testing Library + `environment: "jsdom"` for `src/features/**` and write ~10 contract tests for the highest-value flows (open book → page → highlight; filter → empty state; pagination; dialog keyboard path; annotation CRUD against a fake transport). That is the whole missing tier and it costs a day. **Priority**: 🟠 HIGH (it is what makes every other frontend fix verifiable).

**Test-only pollution**: the `MockDataStore` is *used in production code paths* (not just tests) — that is the inverse of the usual problem and is tracked as `lib/mockData.ts` in the bundle (FE-HIGH-4).

## Types

✅ Strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, zero `any` (lint-enforced at `error`), Rust typed IDs, `shared-types` as the single TS↔Rust contract. **No type gymnastics found.** One structural gap: IPC command names are **string literals at 109 call sites with no shared registry**, so a renamed Rust command fails at runtime, not at compile time. A `const COMMANDS` map (or a generated union from the Rust command list) would convert that class of drift into a compile error. **Priority**: 🟡 Medium, high leverage.

## Configuration

- `tsconfig.base.json` + per-package: coherent, strict.
- `eslint.config.mjs`: high-signal; `no-explicit-any` now `error` (**CQ-10 remediated**); one real architecture rule for app→package imports.
- `deny.toml` + pinned `packageManager`: good.
- Vite: no `manualChunks`, no bundle budget, `sourcemap` only under `TAURI_DEBUG` — meaning **production crash reports (were they to exist) would have no usable stack**. Cheap fix, pairs with FE-CRIT-1.
- Feature flags: none; the `enable*` flags that look like them are dead.
- No secrets in the repo (checked: no `.env`, no keys; the only sensitive-in-principle surface is local file paths handled in Rust).

## Dependencies

No vulnerable/stale signals found by this audit (no `pnpm audit` regressions reported by the prior run). Two **unused** declared dev dependencies: `playwright` (root + app, no config/no specs) and `jsdom` (no test uses it). One **over-scoped** dependency: `pdfjs-dist` v6 is ~2.2 MB of worker plus eager main-thread code for an app whose primary format is EPUB. Do not remove; do **lazy-load** it (FE-HIGH-4).

## Organization

Good feature-first folders; the misplacements are: fixture data in `src/lib`, a test bridge binary inside `src-tauri/src/bin`, a verification script duplicated at two levels, and `styles/index.css` acting as five files' worth of concerns. No utility dumping ground was found in `shared/`/`utils/` (a common failure this repo has avoided).

## Architecture Fitness

- Rust: **enforced and passing** (dependency direction, cycle, coverage-of-policy). ✅ *Fixed since prior audit.*
- Frontend: **not enforced** beyond the package-entry-point rule. Specifically unenforced: feature→feature boundaries, that new UI cannot bypass the DI transport, that every interactive element is keyboard reachable (could be a lint rule via `jsx-a11y`), and that no new colour literal enters a component (lint-able via a regex on arbitrary values).

## Code Generation

None. `apps/desktop/src-tauri/gen/schemas/*` is Tauri-generated config schema (expected, not hand-edited). No generated-code ownership hazard.

## Legacy

None in the classic sense (young codebase). The closest things to "legacy" are: the mock/localStorage fallback path (`tauri.ts`, kept for the web-dev/test experience but now a permanent dual-mode), the `LUMA-OPEN` debug trace layer, and the `reader-highlight`/`reader-highlight-amber` CSS marked "Legacy" in `index.css` alongside the live `mark.luma-highlight` system. All three are removable with low risk.

### ❌ CQ-CRIT-1 🆕 — The test suite rewrites a git-tracked documentation artifact

**Evidence (reproduced during this audit)**: `apps/desktop/src/lib/__tests__/runtimeTelemetryCapture.test.ts:126-132` resolves `path.resolve(__dirname, "../../../../../docs/performance/runtime")`, `mkdirSync`s it and `writeFileSync`s `raw_telemetry_capture.json`. Running `pnpm test` produced a **235-insertion / 235-deletion diff** on that tracked file (new `benchmark_date` + re-measured statistics). The file is the project's *committed performance evidence*.
**Observed pain**: every engineer who runs the test suite gets a dirty working tree on an unrelated file; the diff is pure noise that will be accidentally committed or will block a clean-tree check; and the documented "raw telemetry capture" is silently **overwritten with whatever the last runner's machine produced**, so the evidence is not reproducible — it is a moving target.
**Impact**: repo hygiene + the credibility of the performance evidence base. Two engineers running tests on different machines fight over one file.
**Correct / honest remedies** (choose one): (a) write to an env-configurable output path that defaults to a temp dir (`LUMA_TELEMETRY_OUT`), and have the docs-capture step be an explicit script; (b) assert the metrics in-process and never persist; (c) if the artifact must be regenerated, do it in a deliberate, documented command (`pnpm perf:capture`) that is *not* part of `pnpm test`. Any of the three makes the suite hermetic.
**Validation**: `pnpm test` twice, then `git status --porcelain` — must be empty.
**Priority**: 🔴 **Do now** (it is a one-line fix and it is currently corrupting the project's own evidence).

## Code Review / PR Locality / Static Analysis / Quality Gates

- Commit history (74 commits) shows small, scoped, conventionally-prefixed commits (`fix(library,reader): …`, `refactor(quality): remediate audit debt CQ-02/04/06/10 …`) — good locality, good traceability to audit IDs.
- Solo maintainer: review-culture findings are not applicable yet. When a second engineer joins, the automated gates (below) already free human review for design/risk.
- Static analysis: strong and high-signal. **Recommended additions** (all frontend, all cheap): `jsx-a11y` rules; `no-restricted-syntax` banning new arbitrary-hex Tailwind values (the 135 literals are already there — a rule prevents the 136th); `no-console` for `src/features/**` (would have caught FE-MED-6); a bundle-size assertion in CI.
- Quality gates: local (format/lint/typecheck/test) and CI (3-OS + cargo-deny) are well-staged. **Missing tier**: any frontend performance/budget gate and any a11y gate — the Rust side has a budget harness, the frontend has nothing.

## Metrics

Signals used here: hook density, file size, exported-method count, dead-export counts, bundle byte counts, hook counts per component, hex-literal counts, a11y-attribute counts, test counts per tier. None used as a target; no LOC or coverage percentage was treated as a goal. **A note for the maintainer**: the repository's own audit docs already avoid vanity metrics — keep that.

## Performance / Maintainability Interaction

Unusual complexity in the frontend is *mostly* justified and documented (PDF text-layer geometry, intersection-gated page rendering, highlight DOM range arithmetic in `highlightEngine.ts` — the last of which is protected by 12 dedicated tests). The one place where complexity is **not** justified by profiling is `LibraryView`'s memoization layer (part of 47 hooks, written before any measurement). Rust's perf-critical complexity is budget-asserted — model behaviour.

# PART III — ARCHITECTURE & SYSTEM DESIGN

## Executive Architecture Assessment

Luma's architecture is **better than its documentation claims and simpler than its folder count implies** — a modular monolith (Rust workspace) + single-window Tauri shell + a thin CSR frontend, with a **correctly placed and now continuously enforced** layering, a real security boundary at the IPC, and a genuine product-differentiating core (the anchoring engine). The system has **not** committed any of the classic overreach sins: no microservices, no premature DDD/CQRS/event sourcing, no Kubernetes, no service mesh, no event streaming, no distributed transactions, no unnecessary abstraction layers. This restraint is the most valuable architectural asset here and should be protected from future fashion.

Three architectural gaps matter:

1. **The frontend has no navigation architecture** (feature surfaces are routed by local state in a god component) — the only place where the architecture will not scale with the product roadmap.
2. **The system has no failure-and-diagnosis architecture.** Rust is robust; the moment control crosses into the UI, failures are unrepresented (no error boundary, no error telemetry, no user-visible error states, no source maps in release).
3. **Capability surfaces exist for capabilities that do not** (`SyncDeviceCenter`, `IntegrationsPluginsView` are backed by static local state; `luma-sync`/`luma-ai` remain unused crates). Product honesty, not just architecture.

**Verdict**: preserve the modular monolith and the crate layering; fix the frontend's navigation/state ownership and its error/failure architecture; do **not** extract services, add messaging, or introduce a state-management framework.

## Requirements & Quality Attributes (as actually expressed by the code)

| Attribute | Requirement implied by the product | Architectural support | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data ownership / privacy | Absolute (local-first, "own your data") | SQLite-only durable store, no cloud, no analytics | ✅ except: Google Fonts CDN request (FE-MED-2) and CSP-permitted remote images from EPUB HTML (ARCH-MED-3) |
| Annotation integrity | Signature differentiator | Rust multi-signal anchoring + canonical model + 12 dedicated harness tests | ✅ strong |
| Latency | Interactive page turns, instant library | In-process IPC, LRU canonical cache, debounced writes, intersection-gated PDF pages | ✅ adequate; no cancellation guards (races) |
| Throughput | Single user | n/a | N/A |
| Availability / durability | Local single-user | WAL + foreign keys + transactional backup + ZIP export | ✅ proportionate |
| Consistency | Strong, local | Single SQLite writer connection; reads on a second connection | ✅ correctly chosen — and correctly **not** eventual |
| Security | Untrusted documents | Path guards, zip-bomb limits, SHA-256, ammonia sanitizer, `core:default` capabilities only | ⚠️ CSP weaknesses; dev bridge unauthenticated on loopback |
| Observability | Diagnosis of reader/highlight bugs | Rust perf harness, in-app in-memory telemetry | ❌ no error/field telemetry; CI frontend budget absent |
| Maintainability | "next engineer can change it safely" | Enforced Rust layering, typed contracts, feature folders, excellent rationale comments | ⚠️ god module/component, tripled theme, frontend boundaries unenforced |
| Accessibility | Not yet stated as a requirement | Partial ARIA in reader/library only | ❌ no requirement expressed anywhere in docs ⇒ treated as optional |
| Scalability | Not required (desktop, single user) | — | N/A — correctly not engineered for |
| Cost | Local, zero infra | No cloud at all | ✅ |

**The requirement gap worth naming**: **accessibility is not a stated quality attribute anywhere in `docs/`**. Because quality attributes drive architecture, a11y was never designed in — which is exactly the observed outcome. Adding one line to `ARCHITECTURE-PRINCIPLES.md` ("WCAG 2.2 AA for all interactive surfaces") would be the highest-leverage architectural *decision* available, because it converts a scatter of fixes into a review criterion.
